chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Ubayd, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him, "What is permissible for a man to see of a woman if she has no mahram (close male relative) with her?" He said: "The face, the two hands (palms), and the two feet."

key_terms.مَحْرَم: Mahram (close male relative with whom marriage is prohibited)

ai.seo_question: What parts of a woman's body are permissible for a man to see according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific boundaries of *awrah* for men regarding unfamiliar women, explicitly including the feet alongside the face and hands. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the feet from other body parts, often debated in relation to the 'draw their veils over their chests' verse. The hadith provides practical legal guidance for daily interactions, ensuring modesty while allowing for necessary visibility.
